[F1] $F_{\mathrm{QG}}$ carries the lower global basis $\{G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\mu)\}$
of [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]:
an explicit wedge bar $\psi$ with vacuum fixed, $q \mapsto q^{-1}$ and
$U$/bar compatibility; the integral triangular correction
$G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda) = |\lambda\rangle + \sum_{\mu \text{ strictly dominated by } \lambda} d_{\mu\lambda}(q)|\mu\rangle$
with $d_{\mu\lambda} \in q\mathbb{Z}[q]$, diagonal $1$, same $e$-core support and
$G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda) \equiv |\lambda\rangle \bmod qF_0$; the full family is
an $A$-basis of the partition Laurent lattice and an $A_0$ basis, and exactly
the $e$-regular $G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda)$ form the lower global basis of
$M_{\mathrm{QG}} = V(\Lambda_0)$; the bar reverses the wedge word and multiplies
by a scalar depending only on the residues of the entries (its unequal-residue
pair count), so it preserves the weight multiset; LT's transpose statement
concerns the bar matrix, not $D$, and the equality
$d_{\lambda\mu} = d_{\mu'\lambda'}$ for all lower coefficients is false.

[F2] The transported basic module $M_{\mathrm{sym}} = J^{-1}V(\Lambda_0)$ has
the $e$-restricted labels as its crystal, and every restricted shape is reached
from the empty partition by cogood additions
([[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]).

[F3] For every finite root/label component of $M = U^-$ or $V(\lambda)$, the
restricted integral dual $M_A^\vee$ has the actual $A$-basis $\{G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)\}$
dual to $\{G(b)\}$ with perfect pairing $B : (M_A^\vee)_\mu \times (M_A)_\mu \to A$;
globally these bases form direct sums and the dual charts are
$L_0^\vee = \bigoplus A_0G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ and
$L_\infty^\vee = \bigoplus A_\infty G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ with balanced
$\mathbb{Z}$-intersection; the upper bar $\psi^\vee$ fixes each
$G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$, the upper operators satisfy the exact mixed adjunction,
and their reductions at $0$ equal the lower crystal operators. This means
restricted graded perfectness, not identification with the full product
$\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_A,A)$, and implies no lower-$A$ selfduality, no $A$-unit
Gram matrix and no equality of upper and lower integral bases
([[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]).

[F4] LLT's canonical basis $\{G(\lambda)\}$ of the $q$-deformed Fock space
satisfies $G(\mu) = \sum_\lambda d_{\lambda\mu}(q)|\lambda\rangle$ with
$d_{\lambda\mu} \in \mathbb{Z}[q]$, $d_{\lambda\lambda} = 1$, $d_{\lambda\mu} = 0$
unless $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $n$-core and $\lambda$ is dominated by
$\mu$, and $\{G(\lambda) : \lambda\ n\text{-regular}\}$ is the lower crystal
basis of $M(\Lambda_0)$; the adjoint basis satisfies
$G^\dagger(\lambda)' = G^-(\lambda')$ for the semilinear involution
$|\mu\rangle' = |\mu'\rangle$. The printed $n = 2$ matrices include
$G(2) = |2\rangle + q|11\rangle$ (LLT Theorem 4.1 and the display after it).

[F5] Each weight space $V_w$ of $F_{\mathrm{sym}}$ is finite-dimensional: independence of the full affine simple roots makes the weight determine all residue counts $m_i$, hence $\sum_i m_i=|\lambda|$ is fixed, and only finitely many partitions have that size. The symmetric form with orthonormal standard basis is nondegenerate on $V_w$. For the particular rectangular matrix $D=D_{\mathrm{rect}}$, [F1] gives $D(0)$ as the matrix of distinct coordinate columns; consequently $D(0)^{\mathsf t}D(0)=I$ and $\det(D^{\mathsf t}D)(0)=1$, so this Gram matrix is invertible over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]).

[F1] The regular labels form exactly the empty component of the Fock crystal, connected and generated from the vacuum by the lowering edges $f_i$ ([[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]], [[thm-the-crystal-of-level-one-fock-space-is-the-good-node-partition-graph]]).

[F2] The datum reflection $\tau$ fixes $\Lambda_0$ and $\delta$ and sends $\alpha_i$ to $\alpha_{-i}$; it preserves all defining relations, and twisting the normalized simple integrable highest weight module by $\tau$ again gives the same normalized highest weight module ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]).

[F3] The conjugation $C$ reverses the content $c-r\mapsto-(c-r)$ and preserves addable/removable polarity, so it mirrors the signature with all residues negated ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]], [[def-good-and-cogood-nodes-by-residue-signature-reduction]]).

[F1] The symmetric model $J M_\mu=|\mu'\rangle$, its node residues, the
weight $\operatorname{wt}(M_\mu)=\Lambda_0-\sum_im_i(\mu)\alpha_i$ and the
ambient orthonormal standard pairing $B(M_\mu,M_\nu)=\delta_{\mu\nu}$ are those
of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]],
[[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]] and
[[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]].

[F2] The restricted lower vectors expand as $G(\lambda)=\sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)M_\mu$, with diagonal coefficient $1$, off-diagonal coefficients in $q\mathbb Z[q]$, and support only when $\mu$ strictly dominates $\lambda$ off the diagonal ([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]], [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]).

[F3] On the basic subspace, the ambient orthonormal form restricts to the normalized highest-weight contravariant form, and its inverse-Gram dual family $G^*(\lambda)$ is therefore exactly the transported upper global basis. It is an $A$-basis of the restricted integral weight dual, with $B(G(\lambda),G^*(\lambda'))=\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$. This form identification and ambient-coordinate construction are proved in [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]], step 4.2; the abstract upper duality and charts are [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] and [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]].

[F4] The empty component is the $e$-restricted component and the restricted
labels are exactly its vertices
([[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]).

[F1] The empty partition has one addable node, of residue $0$, and no removable nodes; hence $F_i\varnothing=|\Box\rangle$ for $i=0$ and $0$ otherwise, $E_i\varnothing=0$ and $K_i\varnothing=q^{\delta_{i0}}\varnothing$ ([[lem-the-node-count-is-the-level-one-cartan-pairing]], [[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]]).
[F2] $F$ satisfies all defining relations of the affine algebra and is integrable ([[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]]).

[F3] For dominant integral $\Lambda_0$, $V(\Lambda_0)$ is the simple universal integrable highest weight module with normalized highest vector $v_0$. If $m$ is a nonzero highest vector of this weight in an integrable module, then the assignment $v_0\mapsto m$ extends to a homomorphism $V(\Lambda_0)\to U_qm$; the map is unique after normalizing that vector ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

[F1] The transported identification sends $[S(\mu)]$ to the standard Fock
vector $S_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)$
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]); and
$S_\mu=\sum_\lambda d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ over the restricted
labels, with the same coefficients as the lower expansion, by
[[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]].

[F2] In branch (C0) the transported normalized self-dual simples $D(\lambda)$
map to the upper global basis vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ under
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$
([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] (2)), and the
simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$
([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (2)).

[F3] The transition polynomials have off-diagonal entries in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ and are supported
on $\lambda\unlhd\mu$ with diagonal $1$
([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]);
the graded module group is the restricted direct sum of the blockwise groups
with forgetful maps $\zeta$ satisfying $\zeta(qm)=m$
([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]).

[F4] The graded Specht module and its basis are those of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the regime is
branch (C0) of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]].

[F1] The Hecke algebra is cellular with cell modules the ungraded $S(\mu)$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]
(`thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular`); the local
finite-cell classification of nonzero-form heads, purity and strictly smaller
shared factors is
[[lem-finite-cellular-nonzero-form-heads-purity-and-shared-factor-linkage]],
with the general cellular definitions of
[[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]].

[F2] The graded structure of $S(\mu)$ is the one of
[[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]]; the restricted and
regular labels are as declared in
[[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]], and dominance is the order of
[[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]].

[F3] The classes of the restricted Specht modules are linearly independent and
form an $A$-basis of $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$
([[cor-graded-specht-classes-form-a-basis-of-the-module-grothendieck-group]]),
the transition polynomials are dominance-unitriangular with restricted diagonal
$1$ ([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]),
and the Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]],
[[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]]).

[F4] In branch (C0) the canonical-basis and decomposition theorems identify the
simple classes with the upper global basis and the graded multiplicities with
the transition polynomials
([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]],
[[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]);
in both branches the normalized self-dual representatives and their crystal
labels are supplied by the duality and crystal clauses of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] and the
diagram duality of `def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals`.

[F5] The ordinary Specht-form dictionary and its unit-scaled form identity are
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`, with the
sign automorphism and star compatibility of
[[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]; the specialization at
$\xi=1$ is `cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary`.

[F1] Deep insertions vanish exactly and the period operator has a finite geometric inverse; loop-commuting nonzero-weight endomorphisms insert to zero deeply ([[lem-the-fock-space-tail-estimates-give-q-adic-vanishing-and-finiteness]]).

[F2] The node operators satisfy all affine relations and are integrable on the charge-$0$ Fock space; the stable prefix action gives the node formulas for every charge ([[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]], [[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]]).

[F3] The integrable highest weight category with finite-dimensional chosen label spaces and support contained in a finite union of downward cones is semisimple: its objects are locally weight-finite direct sums of simple integrable highest weight modules. The decomposition uses the Axiom of Choice as declared by the supplier ([[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
